samuel2.17.p1.b1.text: “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David …”

samuel2.17.p1.b2.text: “I will attack him while he is weak and weary … I will strike down only the king …”

samuel2.17.p1.b3.text: This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.

samuel2.17.p2.b1.text: “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”

samuel2.17.p2.b2.text: “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”

samuel2.17.p2.b3.text: “They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs …”

samuel2.17.p2.b4.text: “Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear …”

samuel2.17.p3.b1.text: “Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba—a multitude like the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.”

samuel2.17.p3.b2.text: “If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found.”

samuel2.17.p3.b3.text: “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.”

samuel2.17.p3.b4.text: For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.

samuel2.17.p4.b1.text: “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.”

samuel2.17.p4.b2.text: ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’

samuel2.17.p4.b3.text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel … for they dared not be seen entering the city.

samuel2.17.p4.b4.text: … a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David …

samuel2.17.p5.b1.text: But a young man did see them and told Absalom.

samuel2.17.p5.b2.text: Then the man’s wife took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, scattering grain over it so nobody would know a thing.

samuel2.17.p6.b1.text: After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David …

samuel2.17.p6.b2.text: “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”

samuel2.17.p6.b3.text: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan.

samuel2.17.p6.b4.text: By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.

samuel2.17.p7.b1.text: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown.

samuel2.17.p7.b2.text: He put his affairs in order …

samuel2.17.p7.b3.text: … and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.

samuel2.17.p8.b1.text: Then David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.

samuel2.17.p8.b2.text: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab.

samuel2.17.p8.b3.text: … Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim. They brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, as well as wheat, barley, flour … honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd for David and his people to eat.

samuel2.17.p8.b4.text: “The people have become hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
